response.sql: WITH type_counts AS (SELECT o.ordertune, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders AS o WHERE o.ordertune IS NOT NULL AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM riskandmargin AS r WHERE r.ordervault = o.recordvault) GROUP BY o.ordertune), overall AS (SELECT AVG(order_count) AS average_count FROM type_counts) SELECT AVG(t.order_count) AS average_count_above_average, AVG(t.order_count - a.average_count) AS average_excess FROM type_counts AS t CROSS JOIN overall AS a WHERE t.order_count > a.average_count;

assumptions.assumption: The average is across order types with at least one matched order; orders without a type are excluded. Each order is counted once even if it has multiple risk/margin records.

alternatives.interpretation: Include all four documented order types in the average, assigning zero to types with no matched orders.
alternatives.sql: WITH order_types(ordertune) AS (VALUES ('Stop'), ('Market'), ('Limit'), ('StopLimit')), type_counts AS (SELECT t.ordertune, COUNT(o.orderspivot) AS order_count FROM order_types AS t LEFT JOIN orders AS o ON o.ordertune = t.ordertune AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM riskandmargin AS r WHERE r.ordervault = o.recordvault) GROUP BY t.ordertune), overall AS (SELECT AVG(order_count) AS average_count FROM type_counts) SELECT AVG(t.order_count) AS average_count_above_average, AVG(t.order_count - a.average_count) AS average_excess FROM type_counts AS t CROSS JOIN overall AS a WHERE t.order_count > a.average_count;
